auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 111, see run record
professional: a senior email/deliverability engineer who has run support inboxes and bulk senders; they check first that the MIME reader decodes what real clients send per RFC 5322 / 2045-2047 / 2046 / 2231 (encoded-words, multipart boundaries and epilogues, charsets, quoted-printable soft breaks), that triage cannot be bypassed by a common message shape, that outbound mail meets CAN-SPAM and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe, RFC 3834 loop rules, that SPF/DKIM/DMARC are config as code, and that generated config matches its generator

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against the RFCs with scratch messages (/tmp/claude-0/email-audit/t1.mjs, t2.mjs) run through mime.mjs and classify.mjs. Pass: all RFC 2047 section 8 examples ('(=?ISO-8859-1?Q?a?= =?ISO-8859-1?Q?b?=)' -> '(ab)', folded whitespace -> '(ab)', 'a_b' -> 'a b', 'Andre' with E9 in ISO-8859-1, the two-charset B example -> 'If you can read this you understand the example.'), RFC 2231 language suffix '=?UTF-8*en?Q?Hi?=' -> 'Hi', nested multipart/mixed > alternative with base64 UTF-8 plain -> 'Hello world' plus emoji, QP '=E9', '=3D' and '=\r\n' soft break in ISO-8859-1 -> 'Cafe is = good ... softly broken'. FAIL (high): any multipart/* whose only text part is text/html yields text '' because the piece after the close delimiter (the empty epilogue, RFC 2046 5.1.1 says ignore it) is walked as a header-less text/plain part and sets acc.plain='' first; 'acc.plain ?? acc.html' then keeps ''. A multipart/alternative HTML-only message saying 'I want a refund or my lawyer will be in touch.' classifies {category: support, flags: []} instead of flags [legal, refund], so the owner-flag guardrail never fires and an agent may auto-reply. Also fail: 8bit ISO-8859-1 body (service.mjs:191 decodes the whole raw as UTF-8) -> 'Caf\uFFFD' not 'Cafe'; RFC 2231 'filename*=UTF-8''r%C3%A9sum%C3%A9.pdf' kept verbatim; QP '=  \r\n' (transport padding after soft break, RFC 2045 6.7 rule 3) kept literally; '=?UTF-8?Q?Doe=2C_John?= <j@x>' decoded before address splitting gives name 'John' (RFC 2047 6.1 says parse first).

evidence.craft: Read mime.mjs, classify.mjs, guardrails.mjs, senders.mjs, service.mjs, worker.mjs, store.mjs (parts), gen_config.py (head), wrangler.toml. Small modules behind three ports, pure guardrail function, header-injection stripped in buildMime, constant-time token compare, HMAC unsubscribe tokens, strict config validation. Defects: CATEGORIES duplicated (classify.mjs:11 and service.mjs:50); cap check then send is check-then-act (concurrent sends can exceed daily_cap by the concurrency); buildMime never folds headers and emits one encoded-word of any length (213 chars observed for a 96-char non-ASCII subject, RFC 2047 2 limit is 75); multipart splitter mishandles the epilogue.
evidence.claims: README guardrails checked against code: replies only to thread participants (guardrails.mjs:56-57), auto_reply false drafts only, RFC 3834 machine detection, caps, compliant marketing path reusing email-ops maySend/complianceParts (imported, not copied: guardrails.mjs:19, service.mjs:43), List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post (policy.mjs:89-90), unsubscribe GET shows a button and POST suppresses, tokens, 400-day log: all backed. Not backed: mime.mjs:3 says it reads 'HTML-only mail' and README says legal/refund/... mail is 'flagged ... immediate owner email' and 'Owner flags block every send on the thread'; for multipart HTML-only mail the body is empty so no rule flag is raised and the block does not happen. DMARC claim (p=none, rua to dmarc@) matches email-routing.mjs:123 output 'v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@marisstella.app; adkim=r; aspf=r'.
evidence.fitness: The job: agents triage and answer support mail while anything legal, refund or security waits for the owner. Plain-text and multipart-with-plain mail works end to end in tests and under wrangler dev per the run record. HTML-only multipart mail (HTML with inline images, HTML plus attachment, several web forms and mobile clients) arrives with an empty text body, so the agent reading via cli.mjs sees nothing but the subject and the owner-flag safety net is off for it; Latin-1 8bit mail is garbled. Customer replies are not live until the owner onboards Email Service (stated). A support lead would hit the empty-body case in the first day.
evidence.domain: Outbound and DNS meet practice: RFC 8058 headers on marketing, CAN-SPAM postal address and sender required before marketing, RFC 3834 Auto-Submitted on replies and no answers to automated mail, DMARC p=none with rua while warming (RFC 7489-valid record), SPF from Email Routing, separate domain for cold outreach. Departures a deliverability/MIME engineer would flag: RFC 2046 5.1.1 epilogue not ignored (the high defect), RFC 2231 parameter values and continuations not decoded, 8bit/binary bodies decoded as UTF-8 regardless of charset, RFC 2045 6.7 transport padding after '=' not removed, RFC 2047 6.1 decode-before-parse in address lists, outbound encoded-words over 75 chars and unfolded headers, Date with obs-zone 'GMT' (RFC 5322 4.3 says generate '+0000'), display name with ',' emitted unquoted (buildMime From line), so 'Doe, John <a@b>' parses as two mailboxes.

defects.what: Multipart messages whose only text is text/html parse to an empty body: the piece after the close delimiter (the epilogue, normally empty) is walked as a header-less text/plain part and sets acc.plain = '' before the HTML, and parseMessage keeps '' over the HTML. Classification then sees only the subject, so legal/refund/security/data-request mail in that shape raises no owner flag and is not blocked from an agent reply. Fix: replace the split/filter with `const pieces = body.split(delim); for (let i = 2; i < pieces.length; i += 2) { walk(pieces[i].replace(/^\r?\n/, ''), acc, depth + 1); if (pieces[i + 1] === '--') break; }` (verified in a scratch copy: the refund/lawyer message flags [legal, refund]; all 38 tests still pass), and add a test for multipart/alternative HTML-only and multipart/mixed HTML + attachment.
No test covers a multipart message without a text/plain part, nor the auth-failure-to-spam rule (dmarc=fail -> dmarc=none mutant survives), so both the high defect and a break in spam triage pass CI.

The whole raw message is decoded as UTF-8 before parsing, so 8bit/binary bodies in any other declared charset (ISO-8859-1, Windows-1252, Shift_JIS) become U+FFFD: 'Caf' + 0xE9 -> 'Caf\uFFFD'. Decode headers as latin1/binary and apply the part's charset to the part's bytes.
RFC 2231 extended parameters are matched (name\*?) but not decoded or joined: filename*=UTF-8''r%C3%A9sum%C3%A9.pdf is stored verbatim; filename*0/*1 continuations are missed.
Quoted-printable transport padding after a soft-break '=' is not removed (RFC 2045 6.7 rule 3): '=  CRLF' stays in the text.

Address lists are RFC 2047-decoded before splitting, so an encoded display name containing a comma ('=?UTF-8?Q?Doe=2C_John?=') splits and the name becomes 'John' (RFC 2047 6.1: parse first, then decode).

buildMime emits a single encoded-word of any length (213-char Subject observed; RFC 2047 limit 75) with no header folding, puts an ASCII display name with specials (',') unquoted ('From: Doe, John <...>' reads as two mailboxes), and writes Date with obs-zone 'GMT' instead of '+0000'.
CATEGORIES is defined twice with the same list; a category added to one is rejected or never produced by the other.

verdict: A well-structured agent inbox whose outbound side is senior work: thread-participant-only replies, owner flags, RFC 3834 loop rules, RFC 8058 one-click and CAN-SPAM footer reused from the email-ops policy, DMARC as code, and generated config in sync (gen_config --check rc 0, 11 addresses everywhere). 46 tests pass and 3 of 4 seeded mutants are caught. It misses the bar on correctness and claims: the MIME reader does not ignore the multipart epilogue, so every multipart message whose only text is HTML parses to an empty body; a multipart/alternative HTML-only 'I want a refund or my lawyer will be in touch.' classifies with no flags, so the owner-flag guardrail the README promises never fires for that shape. 8bit non-UTF-8 bodies are garbled and RFC 2231 filenames are not decoded. The epilogue fix is four lines (mime.mjs:112) and keeps the suite green; with it and a test, correctness and claims would reach 3.
